RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT

This Residential Lease Agreement (the "Lease") is made between Ilse Brandt (the "Owner") and Priya Raman (the "Resident") for the home described below. This writing is the whole agreement between the Owner and the Resident, and nothing outside it forms part of what either of them owes the other.

1. THE HOME

1.1 The Owner rents to the Resident the second-floor apartment at 27 Larkin Way, Ashgrove, together with the back porch that opens off the kitchen.

1.2 The home is rented for the Resident and the Resident's household to live in.

1.3 The home is rented unfurnished, and it comes with a refrigerator, a gas range, a dishwasher, and a washing machine in the hall closet.

1.4 The Owner will clean the home and change the locks before the Resident moves in.

1.5 The Owner and the Resident will walk through the home together on the first day and write down its condition on a shared sheet that both of them sign and keep a copy of.

2. HOW LONG THE LEASE RUNS

2.1 The Term of this Lease begins on June 1, 2027 and ends on May 31, 2028.

2.2 The Resident may keep living in the home after May 31, 2028 on the same terms, month to month, until either the Owner or the Resident gives the other thirty (30) days written notice.

2.3 The Owner will deliver the keys to the Resident on the first day of the Term.

2.4 If the home is not ready on the first day of the Term, rent does not start until the day the Resident can move in.

3. RENT

3.1 The rent is $1,780 per month for the whole Term.

3.2 Rent is due on the first day of each month and may be paid by bank transfer, by check, or in cash with a written receipt.

3.3 Rent paid by the fifth day of the month is on time, and this Lease adds no charge for rent that arrives within those first five days.

3.4 The Resident may pay several months at once if that is easier, and doing so does not change anything else in this Lease.

3.5 If the Resident's pay date moves, the Owner will consider a different monthly due date in writing at no cost to the Resident.

4. HOW THE RENT CAN CHANGE

4.1 The rent stated in section 3.1 does not change at any time during the Term.

4.2 The Owner may offer the Resident a renewal, and any change in rent must be stated in that written offer.

4.3 The Owner will deliver any renewal offer at least sixty (60) days before the Term ends, so that the Resident has time to decide.

4.4 The Resident may decline a renewal offer for any reason, and declining it costs the Resident nothing.

4.5 No charge of any kind may be added to the rent during the Term unless the Resident agrees to it in writing first.

5. DEPOSIT

5.1 The Resident pays a deposit of $1,780, which the Owner holds in a separate account for the Resident.

5.2 The Owner may take from the deposit only unpaid rent and the cost of damage beyond ordinary wear and tear.

5.3 Ordinary wear and tear includes faded paint, worn carpet, small nail holes, and marks that come from living in the home normally.

5.4 The Owner will send the Resident the deposit balance and an itemized written list of anything taken out of it within fourteen (14) days after the Resident moves out.

5.5 If the Owner sends no list within those fourteen days, the Owner returns the whole deposit.

5.6 The condition sheet signed on the first day is what the Owner and the Resident compare the home against at move-out.

6. UTILITIES

6.1 The Resident pays for electricity, gas, and internet service at the home.

6.2 The Owner pays for water, sewer service, trash collection, and recycling collection.

6.3 The Owner will tell the Resident in writing at least three (3) days before any planned interruption of a service the Owner pays for.

6.4 The gas and electric accounts are in the Resident's name, and the Owner will sign whatever the utility company needs to make that happen.

7. LIVING IN THE HOME

7.1 The Resident may live in the home in the ordinary way and may have guests.

7.2 The Resident may keep pets, and this Lease adds no pet deposit and no monthly pet rent.

7.3 The Resident may hang pictures, shelves, and curtain rods, and the nail holes that come from doing so are ordinary wear and tear.

7.4 The Resident may paint any room a color of the Resident's choosing and does not have to paint it back at move-out.

7.5 The Resident may grow vegetables in the raised bed at the south end of the yard, and whatever grows there belongs to the Resident.

7.6 Neighbors in this building have long left a shared umbrella in the stand by the front door, and the Resident is welcome to borrow it and to add one of their own.

7.7 The Owner will leave a printed neighborhood map and a list of nearby grocery stores on the kitchen counter before move-in day.

7.8 Quiet hours in the building run from ten at night until seven in the morning, and the Resident and the Owner both keep to them.

8. PARKING, STORAGE, AND LAUNDRY

8.1 The Resident may use the driveway space behind the building at no additional charge.

8.2 The Resident may use the storage shelves in the basement marked for the second floor.

8.3 The washing machine in the hall closet is for the Resident's use and costs nothing to run beyond the Resident's own electricity.

8.4 Bicycles may be kept on the back porch or in the basement, whichever the Resident prefers.

9. ENTRY AND THE RESIDENT'S PRIVACY

9.1 The Owner will give the Resident at least forty-eight (48) hours written notice before entering the home.

9.2 The Owner will enter only between nine in the morning and six in the evening, and only on a day the Resident has agreed to.

9.3 The Resident may ask to be present whenever the Owner enters, and the Owner will arrange the visit so that the Resident can be there.

9.4 The Owner may enter without notice only when there is an immediate threat to someone's safety or to the building, and the Owner will tell the Resident the same day what happened and why.

9.5 The Owner does not keep a copy of any lock the Resident adds, and the Resident may add a lock to the bedroom door.

9.6 The Owner will not show the home to anyone else during the last sixty days of the Term without first agreeing the days and hours with the Resident.

10. ENDING THE LEASE EARLY

10.1 The Resident may end this Lease at any time by giving the Owner sixty (60) days written notice.

10.2 A Resident who gives that notice owes rent only through the last day of the notice period and owes no fee, penalty, or further rent after that day.

10.3 If the Resident finds someone to take over the home and the Owner agrees to that person, the Resident's rent obligation ends on the day the new resident's lease begins.

10.4 The Owner charges nothing for handling a transfer of this Lease to another person.

10.5 The Owner may end this Lease before the Term ends only with sixty (60) days written notice and only if the Owner or a member of the Owner's family will live in the home.

10.6 If the Owner ends the Lease under section 10.5, the Owner pays the Resident one month of rent toward the cost of moving.

11. MOVING OUT

11.1 The Resident returns the keys to the Owner on the last day of the Term or the last day of the notice period, whichever comes first.

11.2 The Resident takes personal belongings out of the home, the basement shelves, and the back porch before returning the keys.

11.3 The Resident leaves the home broom clean, and the Owner asks for nothing more than that.

11.4 The Resident gives the Owner an address for the deposit letter, and may send it by email.

11.5 The Owner and the Resident walk through the home together at move-out if the Resident wants to, and the Resident may bring someone along.

12. NOTICES

12.1 The Owner and the Resident may send each other notices by hand, by mail, or by email to the addresses written on the signature page.

12.2 A notice sent by email is effective on the day the sender sends it.

12.3 Either the Owner or the Resident may change an address for notices by telling the other in writing.

13. GENERAL TERMS

13.1 This Lease is written in plain language on purpose, and the Owner will explain any part of it the Resident asks about before signing.

13.2 Anything the Owner and the Resident agree to change must be written down and signed by both of them.

13.3 The headings in this Lease are only there to help the reader find things.

13.4 The Owner and the Resident each keep a signed copy of this Lease.

13.5 The Owner and the Resident have both read this Lease from beginning to end before signing it.

SIGNATURES
